Date: 2025-04-18
Start: 15:05 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Marcus Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Ethan Ward (Redwood), Salma Ruiz (NebulaForge), Tom Brewer (NebulaForge), Ibrahim Khan (NebulaForge), Jae Park (NebulaForge)

summary: Technical sync to align on marketplace listing requirements, VPC/connectivity patterns for a telemetry pilot, and quantization/observability trade-offs. Agreed next steps around pilot scheduling, connectivity diagram, and KMS/HSM confirmations.
topics: Marketplace listing checklist; VPC peering vs private link; KMS/HSM and data residency; telemetry instrumentation and metrics to collect; quantization effects on latency and accuracy; pilot run plan and success criteria.
transcript:
[00:00] Marcus: Okay, hey everyone, thanks for joining. We, uh, we're on 15:05 UTC, I think we'll run about 45ish minutes. Marcus from Redwood here, I'm the AE on the account. Priya and Ethan are with me.
[00:18] Salma: Thanks Marcus. Salma here, Head of Platform at NebulaForge. We have Tom, Ibrahim, and Jae on the call too. Trying to keep this tight — we have compliance gating plus marketplace listing requirements to align.
[00:33] Priya: Cool, quick goals for today: one, confirm networking pattern for the pilot (VPC peering or PrivateLink); two, telemetry collection plan and what metrics Redwood needs; three, KMS/HSM constraints for keys; and four, pilot timeline and success criteria.
[00:50] Tom: Sounds good. For context, we're in a mix of commercial and US-Gov accounts; this pilot will land in our gov account first so we need that compatibility. We're currently using a transit VPC architecture, but we can do peering for the pilot if that's easier.
[01:06] Ethan: Quick note — Redwood supports both peering and PrivateLink variants. PrivateLink reduces blast radius and is our recommended path for marketplace listings where you want fine-grained control. Peering is simpler for throughput but you have to manage route tables carefully.
[01:23] Ibrahim: On KMS — we have a customer-managed KMS setup and use HSM-backed keys for secrets. We need to know whether Redwood will rotate keys or if we're the authority.
[01:34] Marcus: Good question. For Private deployments we typically integrate with customer KMS via our connector; for hosted marketplace listing pilots, the pattern is to use customer-managed keys in a bring-your-own-KMS flow. We don't take custody of raw keys. There might be a short onboarding step to validate key policies.
[01:52] Salma: Ok, so we need an RFC for the key handshake. Also telemetry: what exactly do you need — just latency and token counts, or more granular traces?
[02:03] Priya: We'll want per-route latency, 95/99 p99 latency, token consumption per request, and KV cache hit rates if you enable prefix caching. If you can, also surface request/response size distribution and model variant used. That helps us tune batching/quant.
[02:23] Jae: How invasive is the telemetry agent? We prefer not to run extra daemons on our nodes.
[02:29] Ethan: No agent required — telemetry is emitted from the networking gateway and via the platform control plane. For PrivateLink you'll see metrics in your collector via Fluent or our pushed metrics pipeline. There's an optional collector if you want really detailed traces.
[02:45] Tom: On connectivity — you mentioned NAT and egress rules. For peering we have to maintain symmetric routing for the KV cache to be consistent across zones. Is that required?
[02:56] Priya: If you rely on local caching, we recommend that edge traffic to our serving nodes be stable — so either route consistently to the same AZ or use an internal load-balancer that preserves session affinity. For pilot simplicity, let's pick PrivateLink to avoid route table churn.
[03:15] Ibrahim: PrivateLink makes sense from a security posture. How about IP ranges — do you need us to open a wide CIDR?
[03:21] Marcus: We'll share a trimmed list of IPs and ports — we can also do TLS mutual auth. The documentation will have the exact SG rules.
[03:29] Salma: Great. Pilot length — we were thinking 1 week of steady traffic to capture representative telemetry. Does Redwood need synthetic load as well?
[03:38] Ethan: We prefer real traffic but can also run a synthetic generator to spike the model to measure tail latency. For marketplace acceptance, standard SLOs are: p95 under 220ms for short prompts, p99 under 1s for typical prompts — but those numbers vary by model size and quant.
[04:00] Tom: Can you explain quantization trade-offs? Our platform team worries about degraded output quality when you push to 4-bit or per-channel quant.
[04:08] Priya: Sure — quant reduces memory and improves throughput but can slightly shift logits. For some workloads it's indistinguishable; for others you may see regressions in rare generative behaviors. We recommend running an eval set for your critical prompts as part of the pilot. Redwood Optimize will provide recommendations for quant profiles per model and sequence length.
[04:30] Ibrahim: Are those evals automated? We have a compliance list of prompts we have to check before pushing to customers.
[04:36] Marcus: We can help run a baseline eval during the pilot. We'll take your prompt set, run it across Hosted and a quantized Dedicated variant, and report score deltas.
[04:48] Salma: Perfect. On marketplace listing checklist — what docs are mandatory?
[04:53] Ethan: At minimum: an architecture diagram, network connectivity checklist, KMS/compliance statement, a test plan for the pilot, and an uptime/SLA mapping. Also a short runbook for failover and rollback steps for canary deploys.
[05:11] Tom: Who signs off on the runbook from Redwood side?
[05:14] Marcus: I'll be the commercial point; Priya will own the technical runbook and Ethan will do the observability sections.
[05:22] Jae: We need a sample dashboard to understand exactly what dashboards to expect in our console.
[05:27] Priya: We'll provide a sample Grafana dashboard and a CSV of the metric names we'll emit. Action: I'll attach the dashboard JSON.
[05:37] Ibrahim: About audit logs — we need request-level audit logs retained for 13 months. Do you provide that or do we pull logs?
[05:45] Marcus: For marketplace listings, audit logs can be exported to your logging endpoint. Retention is configurable on the customer's side. We'll produce signed event logs and an append-only audit trail.
[05:56] Salma: Also need to confirm data residency for US-Gov — everything must stay in the US-Gov region.
[06:02] Ethan: Redwood has a US-Gov hosting zone; for the pilot we'll spin up endpoints in that region. We'll document region tags for the marketplace listing.
[06:12] Tom: Anything around SSO and RBAC? Integrations with our IdP?
[06:16] Priya: We integrate with SAML/SSO for console access and support role-based policies. For the initial pilot your engineers can use token-based access, and we can follow up to wire SAML with your IdP.
[06:28] Jae: Okay, timeline question — we want to stand up connectivity this week if possible. Is that realistic?
[06:33] Marcus: If we get your CIDRs and the govcloud account IDs today, we can provision the PrivateLink endpoint and share the SG rules in 48 hours.
[06:42] Tom: I'll send the CIDRs by EOD.
[06:45] Ibrahim: Regarding encryption at rest — are you requiring us to rotate keys monthly? Our policy is 90 days.
[06:51] Marcus: We can align with your rotation policy; just need the KMS policy to allow Redwood's connector role to perform necessary encrypt/decrypt but not export keys.
[07:02] Salma: For the pilot acceptance criteria — what are the measurable items?
[07:06] Priya: Proposed acceptance: 1) Telemetry collected for one week with baseline metrics populated; 2) Quant eval run comparing hosted vs quantized model with less than X% delta in perplexity (we'll propose the threshold); 3) Successful PrivateLink traffic with <1% error rate; 4) Runbook and dashboard delivered.
[07:26] Ethan: We'll propose the perplexity delta and/or semantic similarity threshold for your prompt set.
[07:32] Tom: Is there a need for certificate exchange for mutual TLS?
[07:36] Priya: Yes, for PrivateLink mutual TLS we use cert rotation via your CA or we can support Let's Encrypt style short-lived certs for the endpoint if you prefer.
[07:47] Jae: Any special firewall ports?
[07:49] Marcus: TCP 443 for control plane, and a small range for data plane ports; details in the connectivity doc.
[07:56] Salma: Anything on cost — how do you bill pilot usage for marketplace listing? We need an estimate to get internal approval.
[08:03] Marcus: For pilots we usually do a temporary discounted usage bucket and share projected per-token cost for both Hosted and Dedicated pilots. I'll drop an initial pricing summary in the CRM and follow up.
[08:14] Ibrahim: Competitors — we've been talking to EdgeServe. Why Redwood over them from a technical ops standpoint?
[08:20] Ethan: Quick differentiator: more consistent production latency across on-prem and hosted modes, and richer telemetry for per-request token accounting. Also policy-driven routing and first-class KV/prefix cache support.
[08:32] Tom: Good. Any gotchas for marketplace listing we should know?
[08:35] Priya: The main gotcha is model variant compatibility — some older quantized kernels aren't supported in the marketplace image. We'll validate the exact model versions during onboarding.
[08:46] Salma: Ok, recap — Tom sends CIDRs today, Priya shares connectivity diagram and dashboard JSON by 4/24, Marcus shares pricing and pilot SLO template by 4/23, Ibrahim sends KMS/HSM contact by 4/28. Pilot week target 5/5.
[09:05] Marcus: Yep, I'll create the calendar invite for a 2-hour pilot kickoff in the first week of May. Anything else?
[09:11] Tom: One last thing — we'd like a short run of synthetic load to observe tail latencies before sending production traffic.
[09:17] Ethan: We'll run a synthetic generator the day before the pilot and share telemetry.
[09:22] Salma: Thanks everyone. That covers it.
[09:25] Marcus: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email with the artifacts. End call.
notes: Pilot will use PrivateLink for gov account to minimize routing complexity.
Redwood to run quant evals against customer prompt set and surface delta report.
Audit logs export and retention must be configured on NebulaForge side; Redwood provides signed event logs.
